### Subject: Opinion on eligibility to carry forward accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation on amalgamation under Section 72A

---

## 1. Purpose and Basis of this Opinion

This opinion is issued pursuant to our engagement letter dated [●], and is based solely on the facts and representations furnished by the management of Vertex Pharma Limited, and on the relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, applicable rules, notifications, circulars, and judicial precedents as they stand on the date hereof. We have not independently verified the facts provided to us. This opinion is addressed solely to, and for the sole use of, Vertex Pharma Limited for the specific purpose stated herein, and should not be relied upon, quoted, or disclosed to any third party without our prior written consent.

## 2. Statement of Facts

Vertex Pharma Limited proposes to amalgamate Amalgam Labs Limited, a loss-making pharmaceutical manufacturing company, into itself under a scheme sanctioned by the NCLT. Amalgam Labs has accumulated business losses of INR 22 crore and unabsorbed depreciation of INR 8 crore. Vertex intends to continue Amalgam Labs' manufacturing business, retaining at least 75% of its fixed assets for five years and continuing the business for a minimum of five years.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether Amalgam Labs' accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation can be carried forward and set off by Vertex Pharma under Section 72A.

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 72A
- Rule 9C


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- CIT v. Select Holiday Resorts (P) Ltd (Del HC)
- Indo Rama Synthetics (I) Ltd v. CIT, (2011) 330 ITR 363 (Del)

## 6. Analysis

Amalgam Labs qualifies as a company owning an industrial undertaking engaged in pharmaceutical manufacturing, satisfying the eligibility criteria under Section 72A. Provided Vertex complies with the conditions under Rule 9C, namely retention of at least 75% of the book value of the acquired fixed assets for five years, continuance of the business for five years, and achieving at least 50% of installed capacity by the end of the fourth year, the accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation should be available for carry-forward and set-off as if they were Vertex's own for the year of amalgamation. Continued non-compliance with Rule 9C in any subsequent year would result in the set-off already claimed being taxed as income in the year of default.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

The accumulated losses of INR 22 crore and unabsorbed depreciation of INR 8 crore of Amalgam Labs are eligible for carry-forward and set-off by Vertex Pharma under Section 72A, subject to continuing compliance with Rule 9C.

**Confidence level:** High, contingent on post-merger compliance
